speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; have you noticed any vomiting, specifically if it is projectile or contains bile?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The tenderness on palpation and worsening fussiness are concerning. Do you notice any green (bilious) vomiting, and has the baby passed any stool, specifically checking for "currant jelly" appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No bilious vomiting or "currant jelly" stool reported, which makes Hirschsprung's or intussusception less likely; do you notice any visible "olive-like" mass in the upper right abdomen or signs of a hernia? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Volvulus (likely Malrotation).

The lack of normal stool passage combined with worsening abdominal distension and feeding refusal in an 8-month-old is highly concerning for midgut volvulus secondary to malrotation. I request immediate abdominal imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_XRay (supine and upright).
